title: 'Ramayana' Becomes First Indian Film to Debut at No. 1 in UK and Ireland
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's Hindi-language epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, tops the UK and Ireland chart on its opening weekend and sets a new record for an Indian film in the territory.
body:
• Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, Nitesh Tiwari's Hindi-language epic starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, has become the first Indian film to debut at number one at the UK and Ireland box office.
  • Variety reported a UK and Ireland opening of £2.1 million ($2.8 million); The Hollywood Reporter India, citing the three days from November 6-8 across 364 cinemas, put the figure at £1.7 million, rising to £2.2 million including previews.
  • Both reports agree the film set a new opening record for an Indian film in the territory, passing the previous mark held by Dhurandhar: The Revenge.
  • Per Comscore estimates reported by The Hollywood Reporter India, the film earned $52.15 million across 38 territories in its opening weekend, ranking second worldwide behind Japan's Godzilla Minus Zero.

Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has done what no Indian film before it managed in Britain and Ireland: opened at number one. Sony's mythological adventure topped the UK and Ireland chart on its debut weekend, according to Variety, which reported takings of £2.1 million ($2.8 million).

The film is a Hindi-language epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari. It plays in Hindi and English, and stars Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Yash as Ravana and Sai Pallavi as Sita. It is the first instalment of a two-part adaptation of Valmiki's epic, backed by Namit Malhotra, and distributed internationally by Sony Pictures.

Two tallies, one record

The exact opening figure depends on how previews are counted. The Hollywood Reporter India reported £1.7 million for November 6-8 across 364 cinemas, rising to £2.2 million once previews are included. On that count, the film surpassed the previous record held by Dhurandhar: The Revenge at £2.1 million including previews. Variety's £2.1 million headline figure does not break out the preview share in the same way, so the two reports are not directly comparable — but both place Ramayana at number one and both describe the opening as the biggest yet for an Indian film in the territory.

Before this weekend, the ceiling for Indian cinema in the UK and Ireland was second place, held jointly by S. S. Rajamouli's RRR in 2022, Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan and Jawan in 2023, and Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar: The Revenge earlier this year, according to Variety.

Second worldwide on its opening weekend

The UK result was part of a wider opening. Citing Comscore's worldwide estimates, The Hollywood Reporter India reported that Ramayana earned $52.15 million across 38 territories for the weekend ending November 8, finishing second globally behind Godzilla Minus Zero, which collected $63 million from 101 territories. In the UK and Ireland itself, Ramayana finished ahead of Godzilla Minus Zero, which the same report put in second place in the territory with £1.1 million from 474 cinemas, or £1.4 million including previews. Variety's chart placed Godzilla Minus Zero third in the territory, behind Disney's Wild Horse Nine in second — a difference in chart position the two reports do not reconcile.

The Hollywood Reporter India also reported a 5-day domestic net total of ₹346.35 crore in India and a worldwide gross of ₹663.90 crore within five days, and said the two parts are reportedly mounted on a combined budget of ₹4,000 crore. The first instalment, that report said, concludes with the abduction of Sita by Ravana, setting up the concluding chapter.

What it means for diaspora audiences

For Indian audiences in Britain and Ireland, the practical point is simple: the film is in wide release in the territory now, in Hindi and in English, after opening on November 5. Whether it holds the top spot in its second weekend — the usual test of whether an opening was an event or the start of a longer run — will be clear from next weekend's chart.
